questions.question: Will people run this by hand, from scripts, or both?
questions.why: The tool should work for its real callers.

questions.question: What would the shortest useful command do?
questions.why: A concrete example anchors the interface.

questions.question: Which commands make a change that users may want to preview?
questions.why: A preview helps people check a risky action.

exit_criteria: Name the main command, target users and common scripted use.

questions.question: Which operating systems must it support first?
questions.why: Packaging and tests depend on that choice.

questions.question: Can users install a runtime, or should the command run by itself?
questions.why: The answer affects how easy installation is.

questions.question: How should users get updates and return to an older version if needed?

exit_criteria: Confirm supported systems, runtime and install or upgrade ownership.

questions.question: Will the command read arguments, a file, or input piped into it?
questions.why: A clear input contract works for people and scripts.

questions.question: Which results should a script be able to read as JSON?
questions.why: Machine-visible output needs a stable shape.

questions.question: What result should tell a script that input was wrong or no change was made?
questions.why: Exit codes make automatic handling reliable.

exit_criteria: Record inputs, text or JSON outputs, error exit codes and safe preview behavior.

questions.question: Where should the command read preferences?
questions.why: Users need to know where to make a change.

questions.question: When a flag and file disagree, which result do you expect?
Does any setting need private storage or redaction in error messages?
questions.why: It should be possible to debug without exposing secrets.

exit_criteria: Set the order for command flags, environment and file settings, with a safe default.
